meta.problem: A weekly digest of my GitHub PRs — merged & shipped, needs attention / blocked, high-impact changes, and a velocity snapshot — as a polished HTML page with an executive summary table.
iteration_log: v1 → v2: founder's work lands as direct commits, not PRs → digest tracks PRs + default-branch commits; stale open PRs collapsed; bot activity excluded

agent.name: pr-digest
agent.model_rationale: Newest Opus-class — the default; judgment on 'major' and 'high-impact' benefits from quality, and a weekly run costs cents.
agent.system_summary: Scans akkireddy-challa's repos with PR or direct-commit activity in the window via the GitHub API (vault token); bots excluded, stale PRs collapsed; writes digest.html + digest-data.json.
never_dos: Never modify anything on GitHub — read-only calls only
Never invent or estimate PRs, numbers, authors or dates
Never include the token or any secret in outputs

rubric_criteria: One self-contained digest.html with an executive summary table and window start/end
All four sections; Merged & Shipped = merged PRs + direct commits grouped by repo and theme
Every PR/commit links to its real URL with repo and author; nothing invented
Needs Attention = in-window open PRs >48h unapproved or changes requested; stale PRs collapsed to one line per repo
Velocity (PRs merged/opened, non-bot commits, contributors) consistent with sections and digest-data.json
Only non-bot activity counts; bots noted in one line; scanned repos listed

vault_credentials.scope: fine-grained, read-only: Pull requests, Contents, Metadata; owner akkireddy-challa, all repos

connections.github: REST/GraphQL via curl with the vault-injected token (not a github_repository resource — the digest spans many repos and needs no checkout)
connections.notes: One owner only (no org). An org would need a second fine-grained token — see NEXT-DIRECTIONS.

schedule.human: Every Friday at 5:00 PM UK time (v1)

cases.name: case-01
cases.expected: First verified run's digest, saved at close as evals/case-01/expected.html
cases.last_verdict: v1: satisfied (accurate, but empty — 0 PRs); v2: running

evals.notes: Fresh data every run — the rubric is the per-run eval; case 1 is the regression baseline. Velocity counts are cross-checked against the GitHub API by hand on run 1.

interface.how: Digest downloaded to runs/<session>/digest.html and opened in the browser; Console for run history.
